blocks.heading: Protecting consumers
blocks.text: Consumers can be disadvantaged by unsafe goods, misleading claims, poor information or unfair treatment. Government can support accurate information, suitable product standards, complaint routes and enforcement. Consumer pressure groups can test products, share reliable comparisons, publicise concerns and encourage better conduct. A pressure group can influence reputation and purchasing but does not automatically have a regulator’s enforcement power. Measures need evidence, access and implementation; an inaccurate accusation can mislead buyers too. Identify the consumer relationship rather than substitute employee pay or lender security.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nela Goods advertises a feature its product does not provide. Accurate correction and a credible complaint route address buyers’ information problem. An independent consumer comparison can inform choice, while enforcement can address the misleading conduct. A worker bonus would not correct the customer claim.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Consumers, capital providers and protection
blocks.text:
Fictional Hela Goods makes a misleading product claim and supplies inaccurate accounts when seeking a loan. A consumer group can publish a checked comparison. A hypothetical regulator can investigate the claims and reporting. Management proposes a general trust-us poster instead.

a Explain how Hela’s consumers and capital provider face different information risks. [8]
b Evaluate the consumer group’s role compared with the regulator’s role in responding. [12]

a Buyers need an accurate product description for choice and use; the lender needs accurate financial evidence for repayment assessment. One correction cannot automatically satisfy both. A checked product comparison helps buyers but does not establish the firm’s cash position. b The group can inform consumers and create reputational pressure, but its findings need accuracy and it lacks assumed regulatory enforcement powers. The regulator can investigate under the stated hypothetical authority and require appropriate follow-up. Use both complementary roles: reliable public information and proportionate investigation of persistent conduct. Neither should be presented as removing every commercial risk.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Consumers, capital providers and protection
blocks.text:
Fictional Nara Tools has incorrect product information and unclear financial disclosures. Verified corrections and accessible complaint handling can address both; management compares that approach with publicity alone.

Evaluate verified correction and complaint handling against publicity alone at Nara. Give a concise plan. [12]

Identify groups: buyers need product truth; capital providers need financial disclosure. Correction addresses actual inaccuracies; complaint handling reveals unresolved effects. Publicity alone may repeat reassurance without evidence. Costs include checking and administration. Judgement: prefer verified correction with follow-up, recognising ordinary business risk remains and different records serve different users.
